schema.label: Air quality: annual mean concentrations
schema.one_row_is: one monitoring site, one pollutant, one calendar year: the published annual mean

columns.name: site_id
columns.meaning: the publisher's site identifier or name

columns.name: site_type
columns.meaning: as published (roadside, urban background, kerbside...); verbatim

columns.name: method
columns.meaning: diffusion_tube | automatic | unknown, from the source's own description

columns.name: pollutant
columns.meaning: NO2 | PM10 | PM2.5 | SO2 | O3 — as published, mapped to these codes only when the source is unambiguous

columns.name: year
columns.meaning: calendar year of the annual mean

columns.name: annual_mean
columns.meaning: the published annual mean; null rows are dropped, not zeroed

columns.name: bias_adjusted
columns.meaning: true if the source says the figure is bias-adjusted; null if it does not say

columns.name: lon
columns.meaning: WGS84; converted from BNG if given as eastings/northings; null otherwise

columns.name: qualifier
columns.meaning: any published qualifier on the figure (e.g. '<75% capture', 'annualised'), verbatim

rules: A monthly or daily value is never averaged into an annual mean by this family; only a figure the source itself calls annual is admitted.
Wide tables (one column per year) are unpivoted by the adapter, one row per year; the adapter records which columns were years.
A blank or non-numeric cell is a missing observation and produces no row.
Bias adjustment is recorded as stated, never inferred from magnitude.
Sites without a stated year for their figure are held at 'mapped' for review.

instructions: For each source, propose which source column supplies each schema column. Use the exact header text. Leave a schema column out if the source has nothing for it — never guess. If coordinates are eastings/northings, map them to 'easting' and 'northing' and build.py will convert. If a wide table has one column per year, give 'unpivot'. If the table is not this family at all (a different subject, a summary, a lookup), say so in 'reject' with a reason. Note anything a reviewer must check in 'notes'.
